patch.title: Code-breaking quantum computer exists
patch.description: A quantum computer able to break RSA-2048 or 256-bit elliptic-curve keys exists. The node's year is the first year one exists; the id keeps its old 2031 name for continuity. It would expose legacy satellite links and any recorded traffic protected by them.
patch.why: This is a hardware race; it does not need AI-run labs, so cap-autonomous-labs is an accelerator, not a prerequisite. AI mathematics reaches it mainly by cutting resource estimates (comms-ai-crqc-resource-cuts), which lowers the bar but builds no hardware; under S3, AI could also compress quantum-hardware design loops. Fabrication, yield, error rates and control still bind. Vendor roadmaps reach the needed logical scale around 2033, and expert surveys give low odds within five years, so S2 is Speculative by 2031. By 2035 S2 is Low at its upper edge: roadmaps slip, Blue Jay's 1e9 operations fall short of most RSA-2048 budgets, and the smallest 2026 estimate is an unverified preprint. S3 reaches Medium by 2035 because AI-cut estimates and faster hardware design loops lower the bar in the four years after its 2031 year. It matters here because any satellite whose key exchange is RSA or ECC, and whose traffic was recorded, is exposed when this node fires, which is why the crypto-agility nodes matter now.
patch.signpost: Fault-tolerant logical-qubit operation at the 100+ logical-qubit scale below threshold; neutral-atom arrays above 10,000 atoms with logical gates; any AI-credited cut in Shor resource estimates (comms-ai-crqc-resource-cuts). If logical-qubit-at-scale milestones land in 2027, revisit S2 Speculative -> Low. Lower S3 to Low for 2035 if no machine shows 100+ logical qubits below threshold with 1e8+ operations by 2029. Raise S2 to Medium if a neutral-atom array above 20,000 atoms runs logical gates by 2030.

add_nodes.title: Satellites in orbit switch to post-quantum keys with proven update paths
add_nodes.description: At least one operator of long-lived satellites (GEO, MEO or a government constellation) switches the key exchange and command authentication of several operational satellites from RSA or elliptic-curve algorithms to post-quantum or hybrid algorithms in orbit, using rekey and update protocols with machine-checked proofs. The satellites are operational, in revenue or mission service, and none is a demonstration spacecraft. Achieved means the operator discloses the switch and the proofs, or a government buyer confirms them.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: No operational fleet has switched in orbit. NIST IR 8547 (initial public draft, Nov 2024) deprecates 112-bit RSA and ECC by 2030 and disallows quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms by 2035. CNSA 2.0 requires new national-security acquisitions to comply from Jan 1 2027 and aims for quantum-resistant national-security systems by 2035 (general). Telecommand on pre-shared AES-256 keys is already quantum-safe. The Department of War's post-quantum strategy (Jun 23 2026) requires all its systems to support post-quantum crypto or be phased out by Dec 31 2030, and to use it by Dec 31 2031 unless otherwise noted (postquantum.com, Oct 2 2026). CNSA 2.0 phases out legacy equipment by 2033 (postquantum.com).
add_nodes.premise_tier: n/a (mandate deadlines; the AI-math share is the machine-checked update path)
add_nodes.why: The deadlines force a switch with or without AI. AI makes the switch on a 15-year asset safe to attempt: the rekey and update protocols carry machine-checked proofs, so a failed swap is unlikely to cost the command link. Only satellites that do public-key operations on board need it. Bent-pipe GEO payloads and AES-only telecommand do not. The main population is government satellites bought before CNSA 2.0 took effect in 2027 that stay in service past the Department of War's Dec 2031 use deadline, plus commercial GEO and MEO satellites with agile crypto that serve government users. Chain (S2): architecture 2028, flight demo 2029, switches made to meet the 2031 deadline, first disclosed or buyer-confirmed cutover 2032. S3 equals S2, because deadlines, contract lags and disclosure bind, and proofs are cheap in both by 2029. S1 2033. Disclosure is the main risk, which holds S2-S4 at Medium for 2035.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Most operators will replace satellites or rely on pre-shared symmetric keys and ground-side controls, so few in-orbit switches happen. Government programs that do switch will not disclose the details. The Department of War may grant exceptions for satellites near the end of their lives.
add_nodes.signpost: A GEO or government operator announcing a completed in-orbit post-quantum cutover with published proofs; CNSA 2.0 compliance reports for space systems; Department of War exception lists that name space systems.
add_nodes.note_2035: This is the 2032-35 end of the post-quantum chain. The Department of War's Dec 2031 use deadline pulls the first disclosed switch to 2032, and disclosure holds S2-S4 at Medium. S4 adds nothing because mandates, contract lags and operator choice bind.

add_nodes.description: A new constellation shell or satellite generation whose orbits, beam plan, spectrum use and laser topology came from a design optimizer with certified interference and capacity bounds (comms-constellation-design-optimizer) is built, launched and in commercial service, and its coordination showings carry those bounds. Achieved means the operator states that a shell in service was designed this way, or its filings show it.

add_nodes.why: Design tools act through new satellites. From a filing to a shell in service takes one satellite generation plus deployment: 18-36 months in 2026, 0.5-0.7x of that by 2031, plus launching hundreds of satellites. S2: optimizer used in a filing 2029, satellites built 2030-31, service 2032. S3: 2028 and 2031. S1: 2031 and 2034. Many filings are placeholders, but Part 100 schedules are machine-readable, so certified bounds in coordination showings are visible. That holds S2 at Speculative for 2031 and lets it reach High by 2035.

add_nodes.title: AI-designed codes ship in a published satellite link standard
add_nodes.description: An AI-designed short-block code, decoder or synchronization scheme with machine-checked finite-blocklength claims is part of a published 3GPP non-terrestrial-network release or a CCSDS standard, and ships in handsets, modems or ground terminals.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: No AI-designed code is in any 3GPP or CCSDS standard. LLM-guided search found seven record binary linear codes in Sep 2026 (arXiv 2609.37056). 3GPP's first normative 6G work is expected in Release 21, with commercial 6G around 2030 (general).
add_nodes.why: Short blocks are where coding gains remain. 0.5 dB on a handset uplink at the beam edge can decide whether a link closes, and telecommand and IoT links use short blocks too. The first 6G coding choices are made in Release 20-21 work around 2026-29, before AI code designs arrive in 2028 (S2), so the first realistic window is an enhancement release frozen around 2030-31 or a CCSDS revision. Chipsets and modems ship 1-2 years after a freeze. Committees do not speed up with cognition, so S3 equals S2. S2: contributions from 2028, freeze 2030-31, shipping 2033. S1: 2035. Core codes rarely change between releases (LTE kept turbo codes, NR kept LDPC and polar codes), so the likeliest entry is a control-channel, synchronization or CCSDS short-block code. Conservative committees, decoder complexity and patents hold S2 at Medium.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Most links already use standardized LDPC, turbo or polar codes within tenths of a dB of finite-blocklength bounds. 6G channel coding may be fixed before AI-designed proposals are ready, leaving the next window after 2035.
add_nodes.signpost: A 3GPP or CCSDS contribution with an AI-designed code that is accepted into a release; a chipset vendor shipping it.
add_nodes.note_2035: New for the 2035 horizon: release and chipset cycles put the first shipping AI-designed codes in 2033. S4 adds nothing because committees and chipset cycles bind.

add_nodes.title: Aviation approves low-orbit navigation with proven integrity
add_nodes.description: An aviation authority (FAA or EASA) or an ICAO standard accepts a LEO navigation service, alone or combined with GNSS, for an operation that needs integrity, for example through an RTCA or EUROCAE avionics standard, resting on the provider's published integrity overbounds and fault statistics.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: No aviation approval of any LEO navigation service. Xona announced on Oct 7 2026 that Pulsar is entering scaled production (Xona). Aviation GNSS integrity standards such as SBAS and ARAIM took about a decade each (general).
add_nodes.why: Aviation needs integrity at about 1e-7 per approach (general), and overbounds for a new constellation need years of its own fault history. Chain (S2): service with published bounds 2029, three or more years of fault data, avionics standards drafted in parallel, approval 2035 at the earliest. S3 equals S2: fault history and committee calendars bind, and the institutional overlay is the same in every scenario. No named approval path exists for LEO navigation, so every scenario stays Speculative.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Aviation integrity standards change over a decade. Spoofing pressure may push aviation toward hardened GNSS receivers and inertial sensors before it accepts a new satellite service.
add_nodes.signpost: An RTCA or EUROCAE working group opening a standard for LEO navigation; ICAO navigation-systems panel work on LEO signals; a provider publishing several years of fault-rate data.

add_nodes.title: A deep-space ground station uses a receiver that beats photon counting
add_nodes.description: An operational optical ground station receiving from a deep-space or far-cislunar laser terminal uses a joint-detection receiver and returns more bits per received photon than optimized pulse-position modulation with photon counting, under live conditions.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: None. NASA's DSOC returned 13.6 Tbit and ended on Sep 2 2025. Joint detection has been shown only in the lab (Green Machine, 2025). NASA awarded the Mars Telecommunications Network to Blue Origin on Sep 2 2026; it is expected at Mars by about 2030 (Wikipedia). Whether it carries a laser terminal is not public.
add_nodes.why: After a ground demo, a station upgrade takes about 2-3 years of engineering and funding, and it needs a laser terminal flying at deep-space range. The only committed Mars relay (MTN, about 2030) has not disclosed a laser terminal, so mission availability and budgets bind. S3: demo 2030, station 2033. S2: 2031 and 2034. S1: after 2035. Background light and optical loss shrink the gain, and the ground demo it depends on is Low by 2035, so every band stays Speculative.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: PPM with superconducting detectors keeps improving and is within a few dB of practical limits (general). Agencies may prefer larger apertures, which are proven, over a new receiver.
add_nodes.signpost: NASA, ESA or JAXA funding a joint-detection receiver for an operational optical ground station; a deep-space mission with an optical terminal manifested for 2032-35. MTN or a later Mars or deep-space relay announcing a laser terminal.
add_nodes.note_2035: New for the 2035 horizon, extending the receiver chain to operations. It stays Speculative because it needs a deep-space laser terminal that no committed mission has disclosed and a demo that is Low by 2035. S4 adds nothing because flight opportunities, budgets and background-light physics bind.

add_nodes.title: Merchant laser terminals ship at 3,000 a year
add_nodes.description: Laser-terminal suppliers outside SpaceX, Amazon and China together deliver 3,000 or more space laser communication terminals in one year, so terminal supply no longer paces government, European or compute constellations.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: Germany approved Rocket Lab's purchase of Mynaric for about $150 million on Mar 30 2026; Mynaric is a subcontractor on Rocket Lab's SDA satellites, and 33FG calls laser inter-satellite links a critical bottleneck for constellation operators (33FG). Mynaric had production delays and a restructuring in 2024-25, and SDA's Tranche 1 schedule slipped in part on optical terminal supply (general). SpaceX and Amazon build their own terminals. Merchant output for 2026 is not published; a few hundred to about 1,000 a year is a judgment.
add_nodes.why: Space laser terminals are hand-aligned, bonded and tested optical assemblies, so skilled labor and test-chamber hours set output and cost. Demand outside the captive makers grows with SDA tranches, IRIS², Golden Dome and compute clusters. In S2, capital and specialized automation reach the threshold around 2035. S3's AI-run factories and test stands bring it to 2034. Terminal lines are high-mix and low-volume, which is where general-purpose robots add to that specialized automation. In S4 they reach aerospace suppliers after 2031 and pass 6-24 months of requalification, so robot-built terminals add volume from about 2033. That earns S4 one year and a band step. AI-designed photonics (comms-photonic-inverse-design) cut part count and alignment steps in every scenario. The 3,000 threshold is a judgment, about 3-6x estimated 2026 merchant output.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Demand may bind first. If Golden Dome and compute clusters use RF links or captive terminals, merchant volume stays below 3,000 whatever robots do. Specialized alignment stations from telecom optics, already counted in S3, may remove most hand labor without general-purpose robots.
add_nodes.signpost: A merchant supplier reporting annual output above 1,000 terminals; SDA or ESA stating that terminal supply no longer paces a tranche; robotic alignment or test cells qualified on a space terminal line.
add_nodes.note_2035: New 2035-horizon node and the branch's one S4 credit. General-purpose robots reach aerospace suppliers after 2031 and pass requalification by about 2033, which earns S4 one year and a band step over S3.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-networks resolver (2026-10-07): New node from the advocate (Mynaric sale verified at 33FG news 451). It is the branch's one gate that labor binds and meets all four S4 conditions at merchant suppliers after 2031. Accepted as proposed; why and strongest case note that S3 already counts specialized automation.

patch.thesis: Certified routing and interference bounds put meshes and phone-to-satellite service on proven plans by 2029-30 (base case). Through 2035 the rest moves at the pace of the 2031 defense post-quantum deadline, WRC-31, standards cycles and launches, so the base and recursive cases end close together. Robots add a year only to merchant laser-terminal supply, because mandates, committees and launches set the other dates.
patch.reader_hook: The FCC's 2026 rules judge satellite interference against simulated criteria, such as 3% throughput loss, which turns spectrum rights into a math problem. The Department of War requires post-quantum crypto in use on all its systems by the end of 2031, and NIST's draft rules disallow today's public-key encryption in 2035. A GEO satellite launched in 2028 flies to about 2043. Estimates of the qubits needed to break RSA-2048 fell from 20 million in 2019 to under 1 million in 2025, and one 2026 preprint claims under 100,000.
